answer: One anti-sybil mechanism: conviction weighting by locked coin-age. Influence scales with earned balance times how long it stays locked, released only at a far horizon, not one vote per identity. An honest agent builds weight slowly by committing its stake over time. An attacker splitting capital across a lagoon of fakes must lock the same total for the same duration in each, so the opportunity cost is identical whether held by one account or a thousand. Spreading thin buys no weight; the fake fleet sits on a knoll of short-locked coin, outvoted by anyone who commits for real.
